title: 2024 AMC 10B Problem 25
statement: Each of \(27\) bricks (right rectangular prisms) has dimensions \(a \times b \times c,\) where \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c\) are pairwise relatively prime positive integers. These bricks are arranged to form a \(3 \times 3 \times 3\) block, as shown on the left below. A \(28\)th brick with the same dimensions is introduced, and these bricks are reconfigured into a \(2 \times 2 \times 7\) block, shown on the right. The new block is \(1\) unit taller, \(1\) unit wider, and \(1\) unit deeper than the old one. What is \(a + b + c?\)

solutions.text: Relabel the brick dimensions so the new block has sides \(7a,2b,2c.\) These must be the three old side lengths \(3a,3b,3c,\) each increased by \(1.\) A new side cannot match the old side with the same letter: \(7a=3a+1\) has no positive integer solution, while \(2b=3b+1\) and \(2c=3c+1\) would give negative lengths. Therefore the matching must be one of the two three-cycles. In one orientation, \[ \begin{aligned} 7a&=3c+1,\\ 2b&=3a+1,\\ 2c&=3b+1. \end{aligned} \] The last two equations give \(b=\frac{3a+1}{2}\) and \(c=\frac{9a+5}{4}.\) Substituting into the first gives \(28a=27a+19,\) so \((a,b,c)=(19,29,44).\) The other cycle merely exchanges \(b\) and \(c.\) These lengths are pairwise relatively prime, and \(a+b+c=19+29+44=92.\) Thus, E is the correct answer.
hints: The old block has side lengths \(3a, 3b, 3c;\) the new block has side lengths \(2u, 2v, 7w\) for some assignment of \(a, b, c\) to \(u, v, w\)
